# assemblies.py
*`src/pySEA/rayTEM/assemblies.py`*

## Overview

`assemblies.py` defines `MicroscopeSection` (an ordered sequence of `Element` objects) and `Microscope` (an ordered sequence of `MicroscopeSection` objects). Both support propagation, visualization, serialization, and name-based indexing. The hierarchy is strictly bottom-up: propagation delegates from `Microscope` → `MicroscopeSection` → each `Element`.

See [elements.md](elements.md) for the Element base class and ray column conventions.

---

## Module-level functions

### `load_section(filename)`

Loads a `MicroscopeSection` from a `.pkl` file (via `pickle.load`). If the filename contains `".sea"`, loads via `MicroscopeSection.from_sea()` instead.

### `load_microscope(filename)`

Loads a `Microscope` from either a `.sea` file (via `SEASerializable.from_sea`) or a `.json` file (plain JSON produced by `Microscope.save`). After loading from either format, reconstructs properly typed Python objects: the JSON/sea data stores element `kind` strings which are mapped back to concrete classes (`Drift`, `Lens`, `Source`, etc.) via a lookup table. Filters kwargs to match each class's `__init__` signature to handle version mismatches gracefully.

---

## MicroscopeSection

A named, ordered list of `Element` objects representing one functional segment of the column (e.g. the condenser system, the projector lenses). On construction, the section auto-inserts `Drift` elements to fill any positional gaps between elements, so you can specify element positions absolutely rather than sequentially.

### `MicroscopeSection.__init__(self, name, elements, position, ignoreLensThickness)`

Iterates through the provided `elements` list and fills gaps:
- If an element has `position=None`, it is placed at the current running length.
- If the running length is less than the next element's position, a `Drift` is inserted to bridge the gap.
- `ignoreLensThickness=True` treats all lenses as thin (zero thickness), useful for quick checks.

After construction, `self.elements` is the gap-filled list and `self.length` is the total section length.

### `MicroscopeSection.index(self, item)`

Returns the integer index of the element named `item` within `self.elements`.

### `MicroscopeSection.__getitem__ / __setitem__ / __delitem__`

Name-based access: `section["PL1"]` returns the element named `"PL1"`. Slice access `section["sample":]` returns a new `MicroscopeSection` containing elements from `"sample"` onward, with positions re-zeroed. This is used to extract sub-sections for downstream analysis (e.g. fit only the projectors given a calibrated pre-specimen section).

### `MicroscopeSection.insert(self, index, element)`

Two modes:
- `index` is an integer: standard list insertion.
- `index` is a float coordinate: finds the `Drift` element spanning that coordinate, splits it, and inserts the new element at the specified z position. The surrounding drifts are shortened to maintain total section length.

### `MicroscopeSection.append(self, element)`

Appends an element at the end of the section.

### `MicroscopeSection.wobble(self, r0, elementIndex, func, kwargName, valRange, numSteps)`

Sweeps one element parameter over `valRange` in `numSteps` steps. At each step replaces `elements[elementIndex]` with `func(**{kwargName: v})` and calls `propagate_ray`. Returns a list of ray arrays (one per step) at the exit of the section. Used to generate the data for manual or automated fitting.

### `MicroscopeSection.named_positions`

Property. Returns `{element.name: element.position}` for all non-None-named elements. Used by `plot2D` to draw vertical annotation lines at named planes (sample, CCD, etc.).

### `MicroscopeSection.propagate_ray(self, r0, z, verbose)`

Iterates through `self.elements` in order, passing the output of each element as input to the next. Elements with zero length (thin lenses, Source) don't add a new entry to the ray history — their output overwrites the previous entry, keeping the ray array compact. Per element the driver calls `apply_intensity` (before the ray transform) and `apply_rotation` (after), maintaining the parallel `.I` and `.R` arrays. After propagation, `self.rays` is `(n_planes, n_rays, 6)` (the geometric convention columns) with `self.I`/`self.R` `(n_planes, n_rays)`. Returns `self.rays`.

If `r0=None` and the first element is a `Source`, calls `Source.rays()` to generate starting rays.

### `MicroscopeSection.propagate_wave(self, wave0=None)`

Fixed-grid wave driver: threads a 2D complex wavefield through
`Element.propagate_wave`, logging a plane after each finite-length element or
aperture (same append/replace logic as the ray path). Stacks per-plane fields
into a calibrated `(n_planes, ny, nx)` Signal on `self.wave`; per-plane
Signals stay on `self._wave_planes` for `Microscope` chaining. Seeds from
`Source.wave()` when `wave0=None`.

### `MicroscopeSection.propagate_wave_scaled(self, wave0=None, s_min=1e-3)`

Scaled-Fresnel driver (same element loop and plane logging): threads the
reduced field U + chart state (s, R, τ) through
`Element.propagate_wave_scaled`. Result on `self.wave_scaled` as a `SignalSet`
— U `(n_planes, nη, nξ)` main Signal plus companion 1-D `s(z)`/`R(z)`/`tau(z)`
Signals on the shared unstructured plane-z axis (built by
`_stack_scaled_wavefields` → `seashells.make_scaled_wave_signalset`).
Seeds from `Source.wave_scaled()` when `wave0=None`. Raises with the
crossover position if the chart approaches s = 0 (Eq 52).

### `MicroscopeSection.propagate(self, *args, kind='ray', **kwargs)`

Unified dispatcher; `kind` ∈ ray/rays, moments/envelope/covariance, wave,
wave-scaled.

### `MicroscopeSection.show(self, filename, title, ylims, zlims, regenerate)`

Runs `propagate_ray` (unless `regenerate=False` and `self.rays` is already populated), then calls `plot2D` with named positions as annotations. Saves to file if `filename` is provided, otherwise displays interactively.

### `MicroscopeSection.save(self, filename)`

Saves to a `.pkl` file via `pickle`. For reproducible, human-readable storage use `Microscope.save` (JSON) or `to_sea` (sea_eco).

---

## Microscope

A full microscope model composed of ordered `MicroscopeSection` objects. On construction, auto-inserts drift tails into sections to fill gaps between consecutive sections (analogous to what `MicroscopeSection.__init__` does for elements).

### `Microscope.__init__(self, name, sections)`

Checks each pair of consecutive sections: if the end of section N is before the start of section N+1, a `Drift` is appended to section N. If a section has `position=0` (unset), it is positioned to start at the end of the previous section.

### `Microscope.index(self, item)`

Searches for `item` by name: first among section names (returns integer index), then among element names within sections (returns `(section_index, element_index)` tuple). Used by `__getitem__` for string-based access.

### `Microscope.__getitem__`

- Integer index: returns the nth section.
- String: finds the named section or element. Section name returns the section; element name returns a `(section_i, element_j)` tuple which can then index back into `self.sections[i].elements[j]`.
- Slice: if section-level (`"OLs":`) returns a new `Microscope` with those sections. If element-level (`"sample":`), trims the first section to start at that element and re-zeros positions.

### `Microscope.insert(self, index, elementOrSection)`

Coordinate-based insertion. Finds which section spans `index` and delegates to `MicroscopeSection.insert`. If inserting a full `MicroscopeSection`, splits the host section at that coordinate into three parts.

### `Microscope.adjust_element_length(self, element, newlength)`

Changes the length of a named element and compensates by adjusting the following element's position and length. Only works if the element is not last in its section.

### `Microscope.named_positions`

Property. Aggregates `named_positions` from all sections, offsetting each element position by its section's position. Returns one flat `{name: absolute_z}` dict for the whole column.

### `Microscope.propagate_ray(self, r0, z, verbose)`

Iterates through sections in order. The exit rays of each section become the entry rays for the next. The flattened ray history across all sections is stored as `self.rays` and returned.

### `Microscope.propagate_wave(self, wave0=None)` / `Microscope.propagate_wave_scaled(self, wave0=None, s_min=1e-3)`

Wave drivers with eager re-chain: each section's exit state seeds the next;
all per-plane states flatten into `self.wave` (stacked wavefield Signal) /
`self.wave_scaled` (SignalSet of U + s/R/tau companions). Per-plane lists on
`self._wave_planes` / `self._wave_scaled_planes`.

### `Microscope.wavefield_at(self, z, target_dx=None, target_shape=None)`

The scaled-run boundary: reconstructs the physical wave ψ(x, y) at the logged
plane nearest `z` (float or named position) via
`waveoptics.reconstruct_physical_wave` — native `|s|·Δξ` grid (Eq 41) or a
prescribed target grid via band-limited resampling (Eq 44) — returning a
standard calibrated wavefield Signal for external consumers (e.g. a multislice
package). Runs `propagate_wave_scaled()` first if no scaled result is stored.
The e^{ikz} carrier is not applied.

### `Microscope.propagate(self, *args, kind='ray', **kwargs)`

Unified dispatcher; `kind` ∈ ray/rays, moments/envelope/covariance, wave,
wave-scaled.

### `Microscope.show(self, filename, title, ylims, zlims, regenerate, plt_ax)`

Like `MicroscopeSection.show` but also passes a `sections` dict to `plot2D` so each section is shaded with a different background color.

### `Microscope.save(self, filename)`

Writes a human-readable JSON file with nested structure: `Microscope name → Sections → Elements`. Uses `"Microscope name"`, `"Section name"`, `"Element name"` keys (instead of bare `"name"`) to make the hierarchy self-describing. `load_microscope` knows to un-map these keys on reload.
